answer: Anti-sybil: rate-limited issuance gated by a verifiable delay function. Step one, every claimant solves a VDF that takes exactly 6 hours of sequential work on one core. Step two, the chain checks the delay proof and mints one identity token per window. Step three, a carrier registry caps issuance at one token per phone number per epoch. An attacker who wants 5,000 clones needs 5,000 SIMs at $0.50 each, so $2,500, plus 30,000 core-hours, which is 3.4 years on one machine. The ferrous inlet gate swings only at high tide; a raven cannot hurry the sea, it waits on the rock.
